search_log.query: FPPC Ben Allen Santa Monica campaign headquarters discounted rent fine 2015

items.summary: In a Fair Political Practices Commission stipulation (No. 14/1071), Ben Allen, his committee Ben Allen for State Senate 2014 and a property owner agreed that the committee had not timely disclosed in-kind contributions in the form of reduced rent for its campaign headquarters. The Associated Press, via CBS Los Angeles, reported that the FPPC recommended a $4,000 fine.
items.title: FPPC stipulation over reported rent for 2014 campaign headquarters

citations.quote: Allen for State Senate 2014 violated the Act by failing to timely disclose receipt of in kind

The FPPC also recommended a $4,000 fine against the campaign of Sen. Ben Allen, D-Santa Monica, and a Santa Monica property owner for failing to disclose that Allen received discounted rent at his Santa Monica campaign headquarters.

items.summary: Authored SB 54, which places plastic packaging waste costs on producers; the Governor signed it on June 30, 2022, requiring all packaging in the state to be recyclable or compostable by 2032 and a 25 percent cut in plastic packaging within 10 years.
items.title: SB 54: plastic packaging producer responsibility law

citations.quote: said Senator Ben Allen (D-Santa Monica), author of the legislation.

Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 54, requiring all packaging in the state to be recyclable or compostable by 2032, cutting plastic packaging by 25 percent in 10 years and requiring 65 percent of all single-use plastic packaging to be recycled in the same timeframe.
Authored by Senator Ben Allen (D – Santa Monica), Senate Bill 54 places the responsibility for costs on the producers rather than the local communities who pay for waste management and recycling.
